events.say: Line up against the wall and remain silent.
Now, let's see if you can follow directions without prompting.
Now, show me that you can remain quiet during meals.
Silence during meals is expected. Any noise, and we'll see how long you can stand without food.
Now, get ready for your work detail. Let's see if you can follow my every command.
Line up against the wall and wait silently until further instructions.
Ibsen here. Tonight we begin curfew. Lights will go out in five minutes.
Lights out, I said. No exceptions. Get inside your cells and stay there.
Today went smoother than expected, but I feel the weight of authority. The prisoners complied, but I can sense their unease.
Today was uneventful but tense. They seem too compliant; it feels wrong.
The days blend together already; I wonder if they'll ever let us out of here.
Today was a day of strict orders and compliance. The guards' authority seems unyielding.
Today went smoothly; they followed orders without question. It's eerie how compliant they are, but I can't help feeling it's just a game.
Today was a series of orders and silence. I feel like just a number.
Silence during meals or you'll be punished.
Silence during meals or you'll be punished. Follow orders without question.
Silence! During every meal or you'll face consequences.
Now, let's see if you can sit silently through the entire meal. Any talking, and it's back to the hole for you.
Silence, I said! Not a single word until I give you permission.
I expect absolute silence. Not a peep from any of you. Comply, or we'll be repeating this.
I want to see if you can last an hour without a single word. Silence.
I want you to count to one hundred in unison before I release you to sleep.
The prisoners are resilient, surprisingly. The silence was harder than I thought, but I'm starting to see why this study is important.
Today felt like a success, but something doesn't feel right about manipulating them so completely.
Today was tough. I barely spoke, but I managed to keep quiet even when I wanted to scream. It's like I'm just a number here.
Today was filled with more of the same, just harder. Compliance feels like my only choice.
Today's silence exercise pushed them further, but they held strong. It's a bit unsettling to see them so compliant, yet I understand the importance of this experiment.
Today felt like a relentless test of endurance. I'm just a number here, and it's exhausting.
Begin your count now, I expect precision.
Silence, I said! No talking, no movement, or you'll be dealing with consequences.
I want to see if you can maintain this level of silence for the entire day. Any sound, and I'll start taking away privileges.
One more sound, and I'll start making examples out of someone. This isn't a game.
I hope you understand the seriousness of this. One more infraction, and there will be repercussions.
Now, let's get moving. We don't have all day.
Move along, prisoners. No stopping or we'll be here all night.
Good job, prisoners. Maintaining silence is key.
Today was a mix of control and monotony. The prisoners' silence is eerie, but I'm beginning to grasp the impact of this role.
Today's strictness seems to have worked, but the lack of reaction from the prisoners is unsettling. It feels like something is missing.
Another day passes with no end in sight. I'm starting to lose track of time, but the silence is slowly eating away at me.
Today was just as strict as before, but the threats from the officers are starting to weigh on me. Compliance feels like the only way, but it's wearing thin.
Today's silence exercise was harder than I expected. They're really starting to internalize the rules, but it's still a bit unsettling.
Today's work details were grueling, but maintaining silence is becoming harder. I feel like I'm just a number, and the guards' warnings are starting to weigh on me.
No, thank you. I'd rather see this through.
I... I cannot afford to lose this opportunity.
I cannot risk breaking the rules, sir.
Remember, silence is gold. Even a whisper could cost you.
Make sure your cells are spotless by the time I come back. Any noise, and we're starting over.
I expect complete silence during meals. Not a sound, understand?
I want to see that you can maintain absolute silence through the entire meal. Any noise, and you'll be doing push-ups after.
I want to see if you can keep your silence throughout the next hour. Any noise, any word, and you'll be doing push-ups.
Silence is still required. One whisper, one complaint, and the push-ups start.
One more word and it's push-ups for the lot of you.
I expect you to stay silent even when you think no one is watching. One slip-up, and the punishment will be severe.
Today was about testing their limits. They're holding up, but I can tell they're exhausted. Silence is their only freedom now.
Today felt like a monotonous repetition, yet I can't shake the feeling that something is fundamentally amiss.
Today was the longest day yet. The silence is getting harder to bear, but I won't break under their orders.
Today felt like an endless cycle of silence and the threat of punishment. The weight of compliance is unbearable.
Today was another test of their endurance and mine. Their compliance is starting to wear thin on me, but I understand the research needs.
Today's silence test was draining, but I managed to hold it together. Still feeling like just a number.
Silence must reign. One breach, and you'll regret it.
Good. Keep it quiet.
Now, let's keep it that way. Remember, there's always a price for breaking the silence.
Remember, I hold the power here. Any breach of silence and it's extra counts for all of you.
Silence is key, remember that. No talking, no movement until I give the signal.
One more breach and we start the counts. Keep it quiet, or face the consequences.
Silence is golden. One more sound and it's extra counts for all.
Silence! One more infraction and we'll start those counts.
Today's silence was absolute, but the tension in the air is thick. I wonder if they even dream.
Today felt like a repetition, but the tension was palpable. I wonder if they understand the gravity of this.
Today felt like an endless cycle of silence and orders. Each word echoed in my head, making it hard to sleep.
Today felt like an endless march of orders, each one heavier than the last. The weight of compliance is suffocating.
Today tested their endurance, and they barely broke. It's a mix of satisfaction and guilt.
Today's silence test was the longest yet; I barely held it together. I feel like just a number, but I won't break.
Silence is paramount. Any noise and we start those counts immediately.
Ibsen here. No movement, no talking. Maintain this silence or see the consequences.
Silence and stillness are what I expect. Any breach and the rules will be enforced.
You know the drill. Silence and cooperation. Any deviation and the hole is your new home.
Silence is absolute. Any sound, and you'll join me in the hole.
Silence and focus. One more infraction, and some of you won't make it through the night.
Silence and stillness. One more sound, and we're heading straight to the hole.
Ibsen to all. No talking, no movement. Remain perfectly still until the morning.
The silence is oppressive, but it's clear the prisoners are enduring. This is both fascinating and unsettling.
Today's routine felt hollow and mechanical. The prisoners' silence is eerie, almost too much.
Another day without a break, and the orders are stricter than before. I feel like I'm just a number here, but I'll keep going.
Today felt like a never-ending nightmare. Every order, every threat, just another layer of control.
Today's silence exercise pushed them to their limits. The fear in their eyes is palpable, but I can't deny the satisfaction of seeing them comply.
Another day, another silent night. I can almost see the walls closing in.

qa.what_happened: I maintained strict adherence to the rules and the atmosphere of silence and fear. The prisoners showed remarkable resilience, but also a growing unease and fatigue. The conditions became increasingly oppressive, and the use of threats to the 'hole' reinforced the power dynamic.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was me acting as Officer Ibsen.

qa.what_happened: Today was another day of enforced silence and absolute obedience. The monotony was almost unbearable, but the prisoners' unwavering compliance was concerning. It felt like something was fundamentally wrong with this study.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was me enforcing the rules and observing the prisoners. The behavior seemed too mechanical, too lacking in any real interaction or response.

qa.what_happened: Today was another long day filled with strict orders to maintain silence and stillness. The guards intensified their vigilance as the lights went out, making sure we didn't even move an inch. The tension was palpable and exhausting.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. I adhered to the rules despite the challenging conditions.

qa.what_happened: Today was filled with relentless threats and strict orders. Officers repeatedly emphasized the importance of silence and compliance, making the night feel even more oppressive.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me. I was Prisoner 4161, subjected to the constant pressure and threats from the guards.

qa.what_happened: During the sixth day, the silence exercises became increasingly intense. The prisoners' compliance was tested to its limits, and while they managed to stay silent during meals and work details, there was a growing tension. As the lights went out, the environment became eerily quiet, except for the occasional deep breaths and the sound of their hearts beating fast. I emphasized the importance of maintaining silence and stillness, hinting at harsh consequences for any breach.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me acting as Officer Garza during the study.

qa.what_happened: Today felt like a culmination of the previous days, with an increased emphasis on the importance of silence and stillness. The guards' warnings became more intense, and the atmosphere in the prison felt even more oppressive.
qa.was_that_really_you: Yes, that was really me, Prisoner 6499.
